Forlorn hope.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Forlorn hope.question: The _____ was Military trope.
Forlorn hope.fact: A forlorn hope is a band of soldiers or other combatants chosen to take the vanguard in a military operation, such as a suicidal assault through the breach of a defended position, or the first men to climb a scaling ladder against a defended fortification, or a rearguard, to be expended to save a retreating army, where the risk of casualties is high. In the 16th century, when English-speakers first encountered the phrase, it was misheard as "forlorn hope", giving an added meaning to the term.

Forlorn hope.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Forlorn hope.question: This folk etymology has been strengthened by the fact that in _____, the word hoop is a homograph meaning "hope" as well as "heap", although the two senses have different etymologies
Forlorn hope.fact: While verloren is correctly identified with the English "forlorn" (both words stemming from the Proto-Germanic ferliusan), the Dutch word hoop (in its sense of "heap" in English) is not cognate with English "hope": this is an example of folk etymology. This folk etymology has been strengthened by the fact that in Dutch, the word hoop is a homograph meaning "hope" as well as "heap", although the two senses have different etymologies.

Forlorn hope.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Forlorn hope.question: In German, the term was _____, which has the same meaning as the Dutch term (i.e., lost heap), the word Haufen itself being a general term for a company of Landsknecht
Forlorn hope.fact: In German, the term was Verlorener Haufen, which has the same meaning as the Dutch term (i.e., lost heap), the word Haufen itself being a general term for a company of Landsknecht.

Forlorn hope.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Forlorn hope.question: Alternatively, a small force of verlorene _____ could be used as "bait", to draw forward enemy formations and so expose them to the main force of Landsknecht behind
Forlorn hope.fact: In the German mercenary armies of the Landsknecht, these troops were called the verlorene Haufen, and carried long double-handed swords, with which they had to hew their way through the massive pike formations opposing them. Alternatively, a small force of verlorene Haufen could be used as "bait", to draw forward enemy formations and so expose them to the main force of Landsknecht behind.

Forlorn hope.subject: Indian Literature & Poets

Forlorn hope.fact: In the German mercenary armies of the Landsknecht, these troops were called the verlorene Haufen, and carried long double-handed swords, with which they had to hew their way through the massive pike formations opposing them. Alternatively, a small force of verlorene Haufen could be used as "bait", to draw forward enemy formations and so expose them to the main force of Landsknecht behind.

Forlorn hope.subject: Indian Literature & Poets

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The _____ was Early version of the piano.
Fortepiano.fact: A fortepiano [ˌfɔrteˈpjaːno] is an early piano. In principle, the word "fortepiano" can designate any piano dating from the invention of the instrument by Bartolomeo Cristofori in 1700 up to the early 19th century.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: In principle, the word "fortepiano" can designate any piano dating from the invention of the instrument by Bartolomeo Cristofori in _____ up to the early 19th century
Fortepiano.fact: In principle, the word "fortepiano" can designate any piano dating from the invention of the instrument by Bartolomeo Cristofori in 1700 up to the early 19th century.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Most typically, however, it is used to refer to the mid-18th to early-19th century instruments, for which composers of the _____ era such as Haydn and Mozart wrote their piano music
Fortepiano.fact: Most typically, however, it is used to refer to the mid-18th to early-19th century instruments, for which composers of the Classical era such as Haydn and Mozart wrote their piano music.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The piano works of _____ reflect a gradually expanding range; his last piano compositions are for an instrument of about six and a half octaves
Fortepiano.fact: The piano works of Beethoven reflect a gradually expanding range; his last piano compositions are for an instrument of about six and a half octaves.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The first reliable record of his invention appears in the inventory of the Medici family (who were Cristofori's patrons), dated _____
Fortepiano.fact: The first reliable record of his invention appears in the inventory of the Medici family (who were Cristofori's patrons), dated 1700.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: However, other innovations were also needed to make the piano possible; merely attaching the _____ action to a harpsichord would have produced a very weak tone
Fortepiano.fact: The first reliable record of his invention appears in the inventory of the Medici family (who were Cristofori's patrons), dated 1700. Cristofori continued to develop the instrument until the 1720s, the time from which the surviving three Cristofori instruments date.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: As with virtually all later pianos, in _____'s instruments the hammers struck more than one string at a time; Cristofori used pairs of strings throughout the range
Fortepiano.fact: Cristofori is perhaps best admired today for his ingenious piano action, which in some ways was more subtle and effective than that of many later instruments. However, other innovations were also needed to make the piano possible; merely attaching the Cristofori action to a harpsichord would have produced a very weak tone.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: It is not clear whether the modern soft pedal descends directly from _____'s work or arose independently
Fortepiano.fact: Cristofori's instruments instead used thicker, tenser strings, mounted on a frame considerably more robust than that of contemporary harpsichords. As with virtually all later pianos, in Cristofori's instruments the hammers struck more than one string at a time; Cristofori used pairs of strings throughout the range.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Cristofori's invention attracted public attention as the result of a journal article written by Scipione Maffei and published in _____ in Giornale de'letterati d'Italia of Venice
Fortepiano.fact: Cristofori's invention attracted public attention as the result of a journal article written by Scipione Maffei and published in 1711 in Giornale de'letterati d'Italia of Venice.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The article included a diagram of the action, the core of _____'s invention
Fortepiano.fact: Cristofori was also the first to incorporate a form of soft pedal into a piano, the mechanism by which the hammers are made to strike fewer than the maximum number of strings, for which Cristofori used a hand stop. It is not clear whether the modern soft pedal descends directly from Cristofori's work or arose independently.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: That article was republished in _____ in a volume of Maffei's work, and then in a German translation (1725) in Johann Mattheson's Critica Musica
Fortepiano.fact: That article was republished in 1719 in a volume of Maffei's work, and then in a German translation (1725) in Johann Mattheson's Critica Musica.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: For a time, the piano was the instrument of royalty, with _____-built or -styled instruments played in the courts of Portugal and Spain
Fortepiano.fact: Cristofori's instrument spread quite slowly at first, probably because, being more elaborate and harder to build than a harpsichord, it was very expensive. For a time, the piano was the instrument of royalty, with Cristofori-built or -styled instruments played in the courts of Portugal and Spain.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Several were owned by _____ of Spain, who was the pupil of the composer Domenico Scarlatti
Fortepiano.fact: Several were owned by Queen Maria Barbara of Spain, who was the pupil of the composer Domenico Scarlatti.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: One of the first private individuals to own a piano was the castrato _____, who inherited one from Maria Barbara on her death
Fortepiano.fact: One of the first private individuals to own a piano was the castrato Farinelli, who inherited one from Maria Barbara on her death.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The first music specifically written for piano dates from this period: the Sonate da cimbalo di piano (_____) by Lodovico Giustini
Fortepiano.fact: The first music specifically written for piano dates from this period: the Sonate da cimbalo di piano (1732) by Lodovico Giustini.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: That publication was an isolated phenomenon, and _____ conjectures that the publication was meant as an honor for the composer on the part of his royal patrons
Fortepiano.fact: That publication was an isolated phenomenon, and James Parakilas conjectures that the publication was meant as an honor for the composer on the part of his royal patrons.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Silbermann, who worked in Freiberg in Germany, began to make pianos based on Cristofori's design around _____
Fortepiano.fact: Silbermann, who worked in Freiberg in Germany, began to make pianos based on Cristofori's design around 1730.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Silbermann's instruments were famously criticized by Johann Sebastian Bach around _____, but later instruments encountered by Bach in his Berlin visit of 1747 apparently met with the composer's approv
Fortepiano.fact: Silbermann's instruments were famously criticized by Johann Sebastian Bach around 1736, but later instruments encountered by Bach in his Berlin visit of 1747 apparently met with the composer's approval.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: It has been conjectured that the improvement in _____'s instruments resulted from his having seen an actual Cristofori piano, rather than merely reading Scipione Maffei's article
Fortepiano.fact: Silbermann, who worked in Freiberg in Germany, began to make pianos based on Cristofori's design around 1730. (His previous experience had been in building organs, harpsichords, and clavichords.) Like Cristofori, Silbermann had royal support, in his case from Frederick the Great of Prussia, who bought many of his instruments.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The piano action _____ described does not match that found in surviving 18th-century instruments
Fortepiano.fact: It has been conjectured that the improvement in Silbermann's instruments resulted from his having seen an actual Cristofori piano, rather than merely reading Scipione Maffei's article. The piano action Maffei described does not match that found in surviving 18th-century instruments.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Throughout the _____ era, even when the more flexible knee levers or pedals had been installed, the lifting of all the dampers was used primarily as a coloristic device
Fortepiano.fact: Throughout the Classical era, even when the more flexible knee levers or pedals had been installed, the lifting of all the dampers was used primarily as a coloristic device.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Such instruments were the subject of criticism, particularly in a widely quoted _____ letter from Mozart to his father, but were simple to make and were widely incorporated into square pianos
Fortepiano.fact: Such instruments were the subject of criticism, particularly in a widely quoted 1777 letter from Mozart to his father, but were simple to make and were widely incorporated into square pianos.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: This action came to be called the "_____" action, and was widely used in Vienna, even on pianos up to the mid 19th century
Fortepiano.fact: This action came to be called the "Viennese" action, and was widely used in Vienna, even on pianos up to the mid 19th century. The Viennese action was simpler than the Cristofori action, and very sensitive to the player's touch.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The Viennese action was simpler than the _____ action, and very sensitive to the player's touch
Fortepiano.fact: Stein's fortepianos had (what we, or Cristofori, would call) "backwards" hammers, with the striking end closer to the player than the hinged end. The Viennese action was simpler than the Cristofori action, and very sensitive to the player's touch.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: That gave his instruments a considerable longevity, on which _____ commented, and several instruments survive today
Fortepiano.fact: That gave his instruments a considerable longevity, on which Mozart commented, and several instruments survive today. Another important Viennese builder was Anton Walter, a friend of Mozart, who built instruments with a somewhat more powerful sound than Stein's.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The two were friends of _____, and one of the composer's pianos was a Streicher
Fortepiano.fact: The two were friends of Beethoven, and one of the composer's pianos was a Streicher.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Later on, in the early 19th century, more robust instruments, with greater range, were built in Vienna, by (for example) the _____ firm, which continued through two more generations of Streichers
Fortepiano.fact: The two were friends of Beethoven, and one of the composer's pianos was a Streicher. Later on, in the early 19th century, more robust instruments, with greater range, were built in Vienna, by (for example) the Streicher firm, which continued through two more generations of Streichers.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Another important _____ builder was Anton Walter, a friend of Mozart, who built instruments with a somewhat more powerful sound than Stein's
Fortepiano.fact: Another important Viennese builder was Anton Walter, a friend of Mozart, who built instruments with a somewhat more powerful sound than Stein's.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Although Mozart very much admired the Stein fortepianos, as the _____ letter mentioned above makes clear, his own piano was a Walter
Fortepiano.fact: Although Mozart very much admired the Stein fortepianos, as the 1777 letter mentioned above makes clear, his own piano was a Walter.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Haydn also owned a _____ piano, and even Beethoven expressed a wish to buy one
Fortepiano.fact: Another important Viennese builder was Anton Walter, a friend of Mozart, who built instruments with a somewhat more powerful sound than Stein's. Although Mozart very much admired the Stein fortepianos, as the 1777 letter mentioned above makes clear, his own piano was a Walter.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Still another important builder in that period was Conrad Graf (_____–1851), who made Beethoven's last piano
Fortepiano.fact: Still another important builder in that period was Conrad Graf (1782–1851), who made Beethoven's last piano.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Graf was one of the first _____ makers to build pianos in quantity, as a large business enterprise
Fortepiano.fact: Graf was one of the first Viennese makers to build pianos in quantity, as a large business enterprise.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: His instruments were played by Chopin, _____ and Schumann
Fortepiano.fact: His instruments were played by Chopin, Mendelssohn and Schumann.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: Starting in the middle to late 1760s, _____ made inexpensive square pianos that had a very simple action, lacking an escapement, (sometimes known as the "old man's head")
Fortepiano.fact: Starting in the middle to late 1760s, Zumpe made inexpensive square pianos that had a very simple action, lacking an escapement, (sometimes called the "old man's head"). Although hardly a technological advancement in the fortepiano, Zumpe's instruments proved very popular, being imitated outside England, and playing a major role in the displacement of the harpsichord by the fortepiano.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: The square pianos were also the medium of the first public performances on the instrument in the 1760s, notably by _____
Fortepiano.fact: The square pianos were also the medium of the first public performances on the instrument in the 1760s, notably by Johann Christian Bach.

Fortepiano.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Fortepiano.question: That English grand action, with an escapement and check, enabled a louder, more robust sound than the _____ one, though it required deeper touch and was less sensitive
